title: Resource ramp schedule vs price-shock simulation
content:
Purpose:
This is an operational sandbox to evaluate how staggered hiring (compensation timing + onboarding lag) interacts with three price / demand outcomes. Use this to pick a headcount phasing that protects runway while retaining the ability to re-accelerate if prices recover.

Summary (top-line numbers, current assumptions):
- Starting ARR (run-rate): $132M annualized (as of 2026-07).
- Current cash balance: $185M.
- Monthly cash burn (base, excluding new hires): $5.8M.
- Average fully-burdened cost per new hire (first 12 months): Eng $29k/month, SRE $25k/month, Product/Design $18k/month, Sales/CS $21k/month.
- Typical ramp-to-full-productivity (billing-impact): 6 months for Eng/SRE, 3 months for Sales/CS.

Scenarios modeled (3):
1) Baseline steady-growth: monthly token demand growth +3% mo, no price compression.
2) Moderate price compression: list prices fall 8% over 6 months, demand +1% mo (partial elasticity).
3) Price shock & recovery: initial list price drop 18% over 3 months with demand +6% due to market competition, revenue recovers to flat only if reactive price restores within 9 months.

Key elasticity assumptions (explicit):
- Short-term price elasticity of take rate: -0.6 (i.e., 10% lower price -> 6% higher token demand).
- Enterprise committed volume stickiness: 85% retained during moderate compression, 60% retained in shock unless we offer credits/discounts.
- Upsell cadence pauses for any team hiring freeze > 8 weeks.

Headcount phasing options (quarterly hires across next 6 quarters):
A) Aggressive ramp: +72 hires total over 6 quarters (primarily Eng + SRE).
B) Staged ramp (preferred candidate): +36 hires with 2-month hiring cadence pauses evaluated each quarter.
C) Hold-and-train: +12 strategic hires (critical infra & customer leads), redeploy contractors for feature work.

Representative phasing table (Staged ramp — option B):
Quarter, Eng hires, SRE hires, Sales/CS hires, Product/Design hires
Q3 2026, 6, 4, 3, 2
Q4 2026, 8, 6, 4, 3
Q1 2027, 6, 4, 3, 2
Q2 2027, 4, 4, 6, 2
Q3 2027, 4, 2, 6, 2
Q4 2027, 2, 0, 1, 1

Cash impact (staging + three scenarios) — illustrative aggregated numbers over 12 months starting 2026-08:
- Baseline + staged ramp: incremental burn +$14.6M; runway decreases by ~2.5 months from current baseline.
- Moderate compression + staged ramp: incremental burn +$9.9M but revenue decline reduces net cash by ~$22M over 12 months; runway decreases by ~4.8 months.
- Shock & recovery + staged ramp: incremental burn +$8.1M but revenue hit (~$45M in lost/discounted revenue) drives runway reduction by ~8.5 months unless emergency mitigation (see later) is enacted.

Operational levers (ranked by time-to-impact):
1) Near-term: Pause non-critical hiring (2–8 weeks) — immediate payroll savings.
2) Mid-term: Delay comp increases for next review cycle (quarterly) — medium impact, 6–10 weeks to implement.
3) Pricing: Tactical temporary promo vs across-the-board price cut — choose targeted promos (enterprise credits) to preserve list price visibility.
4) Product throttles: Rate-limit low-value embedding endpoints to reduce token burn on free tiers.
5) Capacity mix: Shift some non-time-sensitive work to cheaper quantized instances to shave GPU runtime cost.

Mitigation playbook for the shock scenario (recommended sequencing):
- Week 0–2: Freeze non-essential hires (immediate). Convene cross-functional working group (finance/product/sales) to evaluate price recovery actions.
- Week 2–6: Pause contractor conversions; negotiate temporary supplier/capacity discounts.
- Month 1–3: Implement targeted enterprise retention credits (not headline list price cuts). Re-run committed volume churn model weekly.
- Month 3–6: If revenue still down >20% vs baseline, activate hiring rollback (stop next quarter intake) and compress operating spend (20–30% discretionary).

Model caveats and uncertainties:
- We assume no systemic regional regulatory shutdowns that would materially impact Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) revenue.
- Elasticity estimates drawn from a small set of early customer experiments (sample size n≈18): high uncertainty ±0.3 elasticity points.
- The model does not capture potential strategic losses (large enterprise churn) beyond committed-volume assumptions; separate deep-dive recommended for top-20 accounts.

Quick sensitivity knobs (how to run rapid experiments):
- Price delta slider: -25% to +8% in 1% steps; measure take-rate and churn in 7-day windows for active cohorts.
- Hiring pause duration: 2 / 4 / 8 / 12 weeks. Compare burn delta and feature velocity (proxy: PR merge rate and deploy frequency).

Open questions (for leadership):
- Tolerance for headline list-price movement — board preference? (ask in next exec forum)
- Minimum viable hiring to keep product roadmap on schedule for upcoming Dedicated launch (must keep core infra hires).
- Acceptable customer credit exposure cap (dollar limit across all accounts).

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Priya: finalize 12-month cash projection table (sensitivity matrix) using actual ledger inputs — ETA 2026-08-09.
- Ethan: produce top-20 account churn risk heatmap (data pull) — ETA 2026-08-05.
- Marta: draft comms playbook for targeted enterprise credits (legal review included) — ETA 2026-08-12.
- Jon: run cost optimization exploration (quantized inference pilot to estimate per-token savings) — ETA 2026-08-16.

Notes-to-self / quick heuristics:
- Hiring cadence pauses are psychologically easy if framed as "staggered patience" with an explicit re-eval at 6 weeks.
- Keep a small strategic bench (3–4 hires) for infra and SRE to avoid regression in SLOs.

Appendix (mini-model snapshot):
Baseline monthly revenue: $11.0M.
Scenario: 18% price cut -> demand +10.8% (elasticity -0.6) -> gross revenue change = (1 - 0.18) * (1 + 0.108) - 1 ≈ -9.6% on revenue run-rate before retention adjustments.
Retention loss (shock): assume 60% of committed renewals hold -> net revenue hit larger in the first 3 months.
